discovery: Aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy enabling sub-angstrom imaging of individual atoms and defects in materials

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Ulm University / Technische Universität Darmstadt, Germany

nominees.name: Knut Urban
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich / RWTH Aachen University, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics (electron optics)
motivation: For fifty years Scherzer's theorem held that round electron lenses have unavoidable spherical aberration, which limited electron microscopes far above the atomic scale. Rose designed a hexapole corrector that could get around this limit. In 1997–98 Haider, Rose and Urban built it and showed that it worked, reaching sub-angstrom resolution. Aberration-corrected microscopes now let us see single atoms, point defects, dislocation cores, solute clusters and interfaces directly, and even light elements such as oxygen and nitrogen. For radiation-damage physics this changed everything. First-principles and multiscale predictions of defect structures in steels, nitride fuels and fusion materials can now be tested atom by atom against experiment. This is basic physics, the defeat of a fundamental limit in electron optics, that became a standard tool in thousands of laboratories. It has changed what physicists, chemists and engineers can measure.
